note: One entry per script page of the PDF, transcribed row by row: the time column, the
motion column, the burned-in on-screen text and the sound cue for that exact beat.
This file is the provenance layer, not the build. Every renderable video that comes
from a script page cites it by sourceId, and scripts/pdf-days.mjs walks both and
fails if a page already made is queued to be made again.
Week 31 made twenty-eight of these pages and has published all of them, under the
older sourceId scheme 'meritbyte-pdf-NN'. That was not visible until the checker was
taught to read both schemes, and in the meantime week 32 was rebuilt from the same
pages — which would have posted twenty-six subjects a second time. Only the two
pages nobody has ever made are queued now: day 17 and day 30.
'status' is the whole point of the file:
shipped  — already rendered and posted. Never make it again.
planned  — queued at exactly one position, named in 'item'.
excluded — deliberately never made. None currently.
'template' is what the PDF table assigns the day to. 'builtAs' appears only where
this repository implements the page as its own composition instead, which two pages
earned: their beats are timed in absolute seconds against a specific body length,
so they cannot be a props file on a shared template.
hardRules: No humans: no faces, hands, bodies, silhouettes, or hand-driven cursors.
No voice: nothing in the audio track may read as a human voice. On-screen text is the narrator.
Sound only: music beds, SFX and deliberate silence carry the emotional arc. Every motion beat has a cue.
Remotion only: every pixel is a rendered React component. No footage, screen recording, or photographs.
readingRules: Text is the script — if the on-screen text does not tell the story with the sound off, the video does not work.
Readability — seven words maximum per card, minimum 1.2s on screen, all text inside the middle 80 percent.
Sync — every SFX lands on the first frame of its motion, never after it.
Silence — where a row says silence, mute everything. It is the loudest instrument here.
End card — every video ends on the same two-second MeritByte card.
Numbers — any bracketed value is a placeholder. Put a real figure in or cut the line.

rows.motion: A text card, plain.
rows.onScreen: We had done the work. All of it.
rows.sound: No SFX. Piano only. Do not underscore it.

rows.motion: A follow-up email thread renders, 4 unanswered messages stacking.
rows.sound: Sent-whoosh per email, each landing on nothing.

rows.motion: A single payment notification slides in. Counter ticks from 11 to 19 days.
rows.sound: Single payment chime. Piano lifts slightly.

rows.motion: Frame holds on 19 days. No motion.
rows.sound: Piano holds. One beat before the turn.

rows.motion: A contract mock renders. Three clauses type in and tick.
rows.sound: Document tick per clause. Strings enter.

rows.motion: A runway graph levels out flat and steady, extending right.
rows.sound: Steady confident tone. Strings build.

rows.motion: Cut to the frame 1 counter, identical, reading 11 days.
rows.sound: Strings resolve and stop on the loop point.

days.caption: 50% upfront is not rude. It is the reason we still exist.
days.retention: A specific frightening number, resolved with a concrete policy the viewer can copy.

days.title: Design To Code In One Minute

hooks.a: Design to working code in 58 seconds.
hooks.b: 58 seconds. Then we show what it got wrong.
hooks.c: This took 58 seconds. It is 70% right.

days.whyItHolds: A speed claim plus a promised critique. The honesty promise is what stops the viewer scrolling.
days.musicBed: Fast clean electronic, 112 BPM. Drops to one held note at 9s for the failures. Returns for the verdict.

rows.motion: A design frame renders. A selection box springs around it.
rows.sound: Music in cold. Soft selection click.

rows.motion: The frame exports. A timer chip starts counting.
rows.sound: Export whoosh plus a timer-start beep.

rows.motion: A code panel streams code fast, scrolling continuously.
rows.sound: Rapid code-stream blips, fast and satisfying.

rows.motion: Component names highlight one by one as they are created.
rows.sound: Light component-snap tick per name.

rows.motion: A rendered page paints beside the design. Timer stops.
rows.sound: Page-paint snap plus a timer-stop beep.

rows.motion: Design and output tile side by side, near identical.
rows.sound: Two comparison ticks.

rows.motion: The output resizes to mobile. The layout visibly breaks and overlaps.
rows.sound: Music drops to one held note. Dry layout-break scrape.

rows.motion: A keyboard-navigation overlay runs and skips three elements.
rows.sound: Flat error blip on each skip.

rows.motion: A bundle-size chip stamps in, larger than expected.
rows.sound: Heavy thud on the stamp.

rows.motion: Static verdict card, two lines, no motion.
rows.onScreen: great first draft. not a final build.
rows.sound: Music returns briefly and resolves. Then silence.

days.caption: A great first draft. Never a final build. The last 30% is the job.
days.retention: Speed claim plus honest failures. Balanced takes get argued about in the comments.

days.title: 30 Days. 30 Videos. The Real Numbers.

hooks.a: 30 videos in 30 days. Every real number, including the bad ones.
hooks.b: I promised transparency on day 1. Here it is.
hooks.c: Most of these failed. Here is exactly how.

days.whyItHolds: Transparency plus a promise of failure. Audiences reward honest numbers far more than good ones.
days.musicBed: Full warm build, 102 BPM. Sparse on the thumbnail grid, a layer per data reveal, peaks at 19s, resolves open at 25s.

rows.motion: A grid of 30 thumbnail tiles fills the frame with a fast stagger.
rows.sound: 30 rapid thumbnail-snap ticks. Music in sparse.

rows.motion: Grid holds. A follower counter renders blurred.
rows.sound: Soft counter blur hum. Music adds a pad.

rows.motion: Counter unblurs with a snap.
rows.sound: Clean unblur whoosh plus a confirmation chime.

rows.motion: A total-views counter animates upward, digits blurring.
rows.sound: Ascending counter ticks.

rows.motion: A bar chart draws, one bar per video, wildly uneven.
rows.onScreen: most of them did not work
rows.sound: Uneven bar-growth swells, deliberately ragged.

rows.motion: Three bars highlight and rise above the rest.
rows.sound: Three highlight whooshes.

rows.motion: The single best tile expands to fill the frame.
rows.sound: Full-frame snap. Music adds a bright layer.

rows.motion: Its first 3 seconds replay in a small inset loop.
rows.sound: The original hook SFX replayed at low level.

rows.motion: The worst-performing tile expands, unflinching.
rows.sound: Dull deflating thud. Honest, not cruel.

rows.motion: A format leaderboard renders, sorted by shares.
rows.sound: Two leaderboard ticks.

rows.motion: A business-outcome metric card stamps in.
rows.sound: Solid low thud. Music near full.

rows.motion: Lesson one types in, full frame.
rows.sound: Text-build tick per line. Music peaks.

rows.motion: Lessons two and three build beneath it.
rows.sound: Two more text ticks. Full arrangement.

rows.motion: A final card renders, clean and still.
rows.sound: Music resolves to an open chord and sustains.

days.caption: Every number, including the flops. Day 31 starts tomorrow.
days.retention: Radical transparency. Reliably the best-performing video in any 30-day series.
